event: Arrived in Vancouver carrying a stolen knife taken from girlfriend in San Rafael whom he ditched
notes: Letter to Roger Zelazny (Dec 1, 1972): 'I arrived in Canada carrying a knife. I got the knife by stealing it from the girl I was going with in San Rafael, whom I ditched, saying I'd be back in California in four days. I've never seen her again.'

event: Guest of honor at Vancouver science fiction convention; gave speeches at convention and University of British Columbia
notes: Letter Sept 5, 1973: 'Shortly after giving my speech in Vancouver, both at the convention and at the University of British Columbia, I decided to stay on in Canada.' Speech titled 'The Human and the Android' with subtitle 'The Authentic Human versus the Reflex Machine'.

event: Had affair with wife of reporter who covered Vancouver convention; offered to fight reporter
notes: Letter to Zelazny (Dec 1, 1972): 'In Vancouver I had an affair with the wife of the reporter who covered the Convention for the Province. I also offered to beat him up.'

event: Had romantic relationship with computer programmer in Vancouver
notes: Letter to Zelazny (Dec 1, 1972): 'I had an affair, too, with a computer programmer who, when I first visited her apartment, asked me two questions: (one) Want to smoke dope? and (two) Want to go to bed? I said yes to both. The dope was terrible.'

event: Had tender relationship with hippie woman named Jamis in Vancouver
notes: Letter to Zelazny (Dec 1, 1972): 'I had a really tender relationship with a gentle little hippie chick named Jamis, there in Vancouver, who was the reason for my suicide attempt. I still sort of love her.' Appeared together on CKLG FM radio for almost two hours.

event: Attempted suicide in Vancouver after Jamis announced she was leaving
notes: Letter to Zelazny (Dec 1, 1972): 'One day we were on CKLG FM live for almost two hours; the next day I heard her mention to some other people that she was leaving Vancouver in a month. The next day I heard her mention... The next day I tried to do myself in.'

event: Worked at X-Kalay heroin rehabilitation center, mopping bathrooms and scrubbing pans
notes: Letter to Zelazny: 'The next day I was mopping bathrooms and scrubbing pans all day at X-Kalay, which is like Sinanon.' Later used as material for A Scanner Darkly novel.

event: Fiancée Francie abruptly moved out, causing severe depression and abandonment of San Rafael home
notes: Letter to Dr. Henry Edwin Bryan (July 4, 1973): 'the girl Francie to whom I was engaged, whom you may recall, abruptly moved out, leaving me with little or no reason for either writing or living. I abandoned my home in San Rafael and all my possessions and went to Canada.'

event: Married Tessa Busby
notes: Letter to Sherry Gottlieb (April 19, 1973): 'On Tuesday we received Locus and saw that we are supposed to get married this week. So we did.' Marriage date confirmed as April 19, 1973.

event: Moved to apartment in Fullerton, Orange County, California with Tessa; phone 714-524-7306
notes: Multiple April-Sept 1973 letters reference 'Fullerton' and phone number 714-524-7306. Move occurred before Christopher's July birth.

event: Flow My Tears, the Policeman Said approved by Doubleday editor Diane Cleaver; scheduled for February 1974 publication
notes: Letter to Diane Cleaver (April 9, 1973): 'Scott had just now let me know you'd okayed FLOW MY TEARS. I'm very glad.'

event: A Scanner Darkly sold to Doubleday (half-finished manuscript); novel based on X-Kalay heroin rehabilitation experiences
notes: June 1973 letters confirm sale. PKD notes in letter to Scott Meredith (June 19, 1973) that manuscript 'got destroyed or stolen during my period up in Vancouver' and must be rewritten from memory.

event: Emergency surgery on lower jaw; severe financial hardship resulted
notes: Letter to Dr. Henry Edwin Bryan (July 4, 1973): 'emergency surgery on my lower jaw suddenly ate up all that we had on hand financially (no pun intended).' Delayed payment of $100 debt.

event: Birth of son Christopher to Philip K. Dick and wife Tessa
notes: Multiple letters (1973) confirm July 25, 1973 as birth date. Letter Oct 16, 1973 to Broxons states 'born July 25th'. Letter to Bob Sept 10, 1973 mentions 'a month-old baby boy named Christopher'. Described in multiple letters as frowning/serious baby.

event: Purchased used 1967 Dodge automobile; plagued by repeated mechanical failures
notes: Sept 10, 1973 letter mentions '67 Dodge' described as 'now and always will be in the garage'. Earlier letter lists failures: transmission, front end, starter, four new tires, choke.

event: Experienced severe postpartum depression; nearly attempted suicide after Christopher's birth
notes: Letter to Diane Cleaver (Sept 5, 1973): 'Right after Christopher's birth I had a post partem, and nearly did myself in.' PKD contacted Orange County Mental Health for crisis intervention.

event: Contacted Orange County Mental Health; therapist resolved suicidal ideation within three weeks
notes: Letter to Diane Cleaver (Sept 5, 1973): 'I contacted Orange County Mental Health, and their therapist pulled me out in three weeks. I never felt such good vibes from anyone before.'

event: Do Androids Dream of Electric Sheep optioned for film by United Artists for $2,000 option money
notes: Multiple Sept 1973 letters. Female reader at UA gave enthusiastic 6-page recommendation. PKD: 'Very shortly, these financial hardships will be over.' Helped alleviate severe financial crisis.

event: Interviewed by Art Cover for Vertex magazine; interview to appear in December 1973 issue with photographs
notes: Sept 10, 1973 letter to Bob: 'he did an interview with me for Vertex which he says, They absolutely are going to buy. It must be true because several people have reported to me that a Vertex editor is wandering around talking about taking pictures of me.' Interview cut from 20,000 to 4,000 words.

event: Filmed for French television production, mostly at Disneyland; exhaustion and excitement caused three-week flu
notes: Oct 16, 1973 letter to Broxons: 'I did two days of filming for French TV, mostly at Disneyland, and the exhaustion and overexcitement sent me to bed with the flu, three weeks ago.'

event: Correspondence with Patrice Duvic; Tessa credits Duvic with helping save their marriage through gentle mediation
notes: Letter Sept 5, 1973 to Marcel Thaon: 'My wife thinks Patrice is responsible for saving our marriage by gently quieting my aggressive violence. In any case we love him.' Duvic had visited about a year prior and did taping with PKD.

event: PKD states in letter to Marcel Thaon that he has been married five times with two daughters and one son
notes: Letter to Marcel Thaon (Sept 5, 1973): 'I have been married five times, have two girls and a new little boy.' Also states 'when the marriage failed I dropped (gratefully) into the gutter of near-illegal life: narcotics and guns and knives.'

event: PKD describes extended period living in subculture with drug users and young people; period of narcotics involvement and criminal association
notes: Letter Sept 5, 1973: 'when the marriage failed I dropped (gratefully) into the gutter of near-illegal life: narcotics and guns and knives and oh so many crimes... I embraced truly vicious people.' States he lived with stilyagi (teen-age hoodlums) and provided shelter to young people who would otherwise be lost.
